title: The Lord Commands Lehi to Depart
summary: While dreaming, Lehi hears the voice of the Lord blessing him for his faithfulness in declaring what was commanded, warning him that the people seek his life, and commanding him to take his family and flee into the wilderness.

Lehi was obedient to the word of the Lord and did as he was commanded.

title: Lehi Exhorts Laman and Lemuel
summary: Standing near the mouth of the river emptying into the Red Sea, Lehi addresses his eldest sons, Laman and Lemuel. He exhorts Laman, saying, "O that thou mightest be like unto this river, continually running into the fountain of all righteousness!" and Lemuel, saying, "O that thou mightest be like unto this valley, firm and steadfast, and immovable in keeping the commandments of the Lord!"
locations: a valley by the side of a river of water
borders near the shore of the Red Sea

explicit_facts.text: Lehi named the river Laman, which emptied into the Red Sea, with the valley located in the borders near its mouth.
When Lehi saw the river emptying into the fountain of the Red Sea, he said to Laman: "O that thou mightest be like unto this river, continually running into the fountain of all righteousness!"
Lehi said to Lemuel: "O that thou mightest be like unto this valley, firm and steadfast, and immovable in keeping the commandments of the Lord!"

Lehi spoke this because of the stiffneckedness of Laman and Lemuel, who murmured against him for being a visionary man and leading them from Jerusalem and their wealth to perish in the wilderness due to the foolish imaginations of his heart.
Laman and Lemuel, the eldest sons, murmured against their father because they knew not the dealings of the God who created them.
